fields.title: Three Kinds of Deletion
fields.keyTakeaway: Deletion is a process with stages and timelines, for transactional data the right answer is usually anonymization, and a promise must describe what actually happens.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A user deleted an account. What happened to their orders?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: A promise about deletion is a legal obligation. An unfulfillable promise is worse than a limited but honest one. Covered mechanically in `DS2-N6-L2`, here — from the side of obligations and design.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **[[soft-delete|Soft delete]].** Marking. Data remains. Acceptable as an intermediate step, unacceptable as an answer to a deletion request.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Hard delete.** Erasing. Breaks links, requires [[cascade-delete-2|cascades]] or [[tombstone|tombstones]] — records of the deletion fact.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **[[anonymization|Anonymization]].** Breaking the link with the person while retaining data. Usually the right answer for transactional records: the order remains for reporting, the person disappears from it.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: What determines the choice — **storage obligations.** Some data cannot be deleted: payment documents, tax reporting. For them the answer is anonymization within permissible limits and honest disclosure in the policy.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: *Main database.* Obvious. *Analytical storage.* Separate system, separate work. *Search indices and caches.* Often forgotten, and the person remains discoverable. *Backups.* Selectively deleting is usually impossible; the answer is backup expiration timeline. *Third parties.* Requires separate requests if data was transferred.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Product-wise important: **deletion is a process, not an operation.** It has a deadline, stages, and states, and this can be shown to the user.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Account deletion as a process with a visible state:
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *Immediately:* profile, contacts, addresses, cart are deleted; reviews are anonymized; sessions are terminated; account becomes unavailable. *Within a day:* deletion reaches the analytical storage and search index. *Within 30 days:* backups expire. *Remains:* payment documents by law, anonymized purchase facts.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The screen shows these four stages with markers — not because the user is tracking, but because it is more honest than a single phrase.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Deferred deletion during an active order: deletion is queued, executed after delivery completion. Explained explicitly.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Cancellation period — 7 days. Came from support: some people deleted their account in annoyance and came back. Over a quarter 12% of deletions are canceled.
fields.sections/3/blocks/5/text: Policy wording: personal data is deleted immediately, disappears from backups within a month, anonymized purchase statistics remain and are not linked to the person.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: The right to deletion has exceptions: retention obligations, establishing legal claims. Boundaries are defined by the lawyer, the product fulfills and explains them.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Deletion is a process with stages and timelines, for transactional data the right answer is usually anonymization, and a promise must describe what actually happens.
